# NPM Improved v1.4.1 — Native in-place updater (no helper containers)

Replaces the updater's temporary `docker:27-cli` handoff with a **native Docker-host systemd service**. The Update screen no longer creates or pulls any secondary Docker container during update, restart, or rollback.

## Changes
- Removes `docker:27-cli` and all Docker API `/containers/create` updater logic.
- Removes the Docker socket bind mount from standard SQLite, MySQL and PostgreSQL NPMi Compose definitions.
- Authenticated Settings → Update queues a request in the existing persistent `/data` directory. A root-owned host `systemd.path` unit launches a trusted installed runner outside Docker.
- The host runner pulls the **NPM Improved release itself** from GHCR, with SHA-256-verified GitHub Release image bundle fallback, and updates the existing Compose app service. It verifies Docker health, control-plane status and version identity, and restores the previous image on failure.
- Rollback and Restart use the same native host mechanism. No updater container is created.
- Host request validation and file locking prevent concurrent on-host update jobs.
- Installer provisions the host updater automatically when run as root on a systemd host; other installations can bootstrap it with `sudo ./scripts/install-host-updater /absolute/path/to/npm-project`.
- CI exercises the restart through the native dispatcher and enforces the no-helper-container invariant.

## Upgrading installations running v1.4.0 or earlier

**The old updater cannot update itself past its own Docker Hub helper dependency.** A **one-time** host-side bootstrap and sequential in-place application update are required for existing deployments. After this patch is installed, subsequent updates operate from Settings → Update without external helper containers.

For systemd Linux hosts, install the native watcher from the v1.4.1 repository's trusted scripts into the existing Compose project. Preserve the project's actual Compose project name, persisted `.env`, `data`, `letsencrypt`, host ports and certificates. Perform the first Compose app-only image upgrade on one NPMX node, verify health, then repeat on the next. Do not update both nodes simultaneously.

This changes **update infrastructure only**. Host Analytics, Node Analytics Center, NPMX 30-second polling and other v1.4.0 features remain unchanged.

**Platform requirement:** Linux host with Docker Engine, Docker Compose v2, Python 3 and systemd. Other host init systems require an equivalent trusted host-side executor and are not silently treated as compatible.
